:::{#def-countable-additivity}
#### Countable additivity ($\sigma$-additivity)

Let $\salg$ be a [$\sigma$-algebra](#def-sigma-algebra) on a set $S$.
A function $\mu : \salg \to [0, \infty]$
is **countably additive**
(also called **$\sigma$-additive**)
if, for every sequence of
[pairwise disjoint](#def-pairwise-disjoint) sets $A_1, A_2, \ldots$ in $\salg$,
the value of their union is the sum of their values:

$$\mu\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{\infty} A_i\right) = \sumto{i}{\infty} \mu(A_i)$$

:::
